newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama to get $45 mln loan for sanitation sector.
newsitem.headline: Panama to get $45 mln loan for sanitation sector.

text.p: The Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) said on Thursday it would lend Panama $45 million to help reform the water supply and sanitation sectors ahead of privatization.
"The total cost of the program is $65 million, with the local counterparts providing $20 million," IDB spokeswoman Christina MacCulloch told Reuters.

The upgrade of the water supply and sanitation systems in Panama City and other areas will be carried out by the Ministry of Planning and Economic Policy and the sanitation operating agency, Instituto de Acueductos y Alcanatarillados Nacionales (IDAAN).
The money will help finance the restructuring of state-run IDAAN to bring in private sector financing and management.

IDAAN will be transformed into a mixed corporation, with 49 percent owned by the government and 51 percent of the stock held by private investors who will operate water and sanitation services in Panama City. The government intends to start the bidding process for parts of IDAAN by October.
"The loan is for a 20-year term with a four-year grace period at the variable annual interest rate, which is now 6.79 percent," MacCulloch said.
(( -- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom, 507-223 7739))
